changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 3 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/6247-option-visiblewhen-metadata-admin.md`

- names `SchemaForm.tsx` → `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/SchemaForm.tsx` — edited by this change

  > Three consuming controls now filter, and each has a pin asserting an option **absent** on a false predicate: the builtin Select in `SchemaForm.tsx`, `MultiSelectWidget`, and `colorPaletteOptions` → `ColorSwatchGroupWidget`. Asserting absence is the whole of the test design — this evaluator fails OPEN, so "the option is shown" is equally the outcome of predicate-true, predicate-never-arrived and predicate-faulted, and a positive-only pin passes against the unfixed renderer.

### `.changeset/console-form-container-specs-one-declaration-5596.md`

- names `SchemaForm.tsx` → `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/SchemaForm.tsx` — edited by this change

  > objectui#5542 converged the LEAF of this contract — the field spec — and left the two containers above it untouched, because converging them was a bigger call than a mechanical import. `FormSectionSpec` and `FormViewSpec` were each hand-declared twice under the same names, once in `packages/app-shell`'s `SchemaForm.tsx` and once in `apps/console`'s `FormPage.tsx`. Unlike the leaf — whose console copy was a clean subset — these two had **already drifted, in both directions**, so neither copy was a subset of the other and there were two live answers to "what may an author write":

### `.changeset/formfieldspec-dependson-5040.md`

- names `SchemaForm.tsx` → `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/SchemaForm.tsx` — edited by this change

  > No runtime behaviour changes: `MetadataField` already handed `dependsOn` through and both widgets already read it. What changes is the type face — it now admits what the runtime has always accepted. The two descriptions are one declaration, extracted to a leaf module (`views/metadata-admin/form-spec.ts`) that both halves import, because `SchemaForm.tsx` imports `./widgets.js` and a back-edge would close a cycle. `SchemaForm.tsx` re-exports `FormFieldSpec` and `VisibilityPredicate`, so every existing importer is unaffected.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `0ffc423b1` (merge-base with origin/main): 3 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1788 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2395 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36680111844)

### ① Derived judgments

**The binding direction is ruling B (`5749198339`):** the declaration surface marks the erasure family; `admitsString()` reads the mark; the husk-boundary pin inverts for MARKED members only; A (a key-name override) stays refused. The diff does exactly that and nothing beside it.

1. **The reader — right.** `erasedAuthoringType()` (`SchemaForm.tsx` head `:453-461`) answers only for a mark that is a non-array object, whose `version` is strictly `1`, and whose `type` is a string or an all-string array; every other shape — absent, non-object, array, other version, missing or non-string `type` — returns `undefined` and the walk falls through to the pre-existing `anyOf`/`oneOf` scan. `admitsString()` then asks `?.includes('string')`, so the mark's VALUE decides, never its presence. A served `object` mark (`['object']`) or `array` mark (`['array']`) cannot be misread as a string arm; a bare unmarked `{}` cannot either, because it carries no keyword and `branch.type` is undefined. The read sits in the one shape test all five detectors share, which is the ruling's one bit read in the one place PR #9911 established — a detector-scoped read would have reopened the split #9911 closed. The array form of `type` is a harmless widening of the reader over what 17.5.0 emits (a string), and it still requires `string` to be named.

2. **The measured consequence — right, and it is what the ruling intends.** On the 4021 served members `admitsString` flips on 50, the widget changes on 45 (all unset to `condition`), the other four detectors change on 0. The judgment point is whether a served form row's `type: 'code'` is an authored widget choice that should win. It is not, under the precedence in force before this PR: `inferWidget()` (head `:337-345`) is documented and coded as "explicit widget, then type-based inference, then schema-based inference", and `resolveFieldWidget()` (head `:912-946`) skips the detector chain only on `fieldSpec.widget`. A form-row `type` yields a default face that every detector has always refined (a `type: 'text'` row named `titleField` becomes a field-ref picker the same way); only `widget` is the declaration tier — the tier the ruling names in "an author pins `widget: 'condition'` in the form spec, which already wins outright". The ruling also expects this outcome: it records that objectui#8167's generic-form arm "becomes reachable once B lands", and that arm is `hook.condition` and the field predicates reaching `ConditionWidget` through `SchemaForm`; had the form-row `type` won, that arm would stay dark for every type except `sharing_rule`. The move from the code editor loses nothing an author had: both faces go through the shared ADR-0089 read/write pair (`widgets.tsx` `#3218`, objectui#10963), and the builder keeps a raw-expression mode. objectui#10963's expression-language path in `CodeWidget` is not orphaned: the five marked members no detector claims by name (`field.expression`, `object.titleFormat`, `job.schedule.expression`, …) keep it, and a producer wanting the editor on a predicate row pins `widget: 'code'`. `sharing_rule.condition` (no served form row) moving from the union-fallback textarea to the builder is the same rule with no form row in the way.

3. **The pins against the ruling — right.** `SchemaForm.erasedArmMark-9830.test.tsx` renders one schema carrying the subject (the served marked `hook.condition`), the unmarked control, an `object`-typed mark, a version-2 mark and a marked arm under an unclaimed name, and asserts through the rendered face scoped by the host label id: subject mounts the builder (ruling: `admitsString` reads the mark), unmarked husk does not (ruling: the veto stays for the unmarked husk), other-type and other-version marks do not (the bit is read strictly), the unclaimed name does not (the mark lifts the shape veto only; the name still chooses — A stays refused), and whole-render accounting is exactly `['condition']`. The second describe pins the declaration tier both ways: `widget: 'condition'` on an unmarked husk mounts (the door the ruling named while the mark was absent), `widget: 'textarea'` on a marked husk is kept. `SchemaForm.nestedAnyOfPredicate-9830.test.tsx` keeps its husk assertion byte-for-byte as the UNMARKED control and renames it, so the inversion is scoped to marked members and the old veto is still pinned. The `ENVELOPE` fixture's `required` list is not read by any detector, so its exactness against 17.5.0 does not bear on the verdict.

4. **The ablations — read as sufficient.** Leg 1 (delete the mark read) turns the subject, the same-render control's subject assertion and the accounting red while the base faces reappear; leg 2 (presence instead of value) turns the value case and the accounting red while the subject stays green — each leg fails precisely the assertions it should and no other. Leg 3 (read a bare `{}` as a string arm) was not re-run; that is acceptable because the assertion is unchanged from PR #9911, where it was proven red, and this PR's code path for an unmarked node is unchanged (`erasedAuthoringType` returns `undefined` and the old scan runs). The leg-1 total (15) exceeds the two pins (12) by the served-entry probe the PR body says ran in the same command; the leg-2 total (12) is the pins alone.

5. **Public surface.** No export of `@object-ui/app-shell` changes: `erasedAuthoringType` and the two constants are module-private, `admitsString` was already module-private, `resolveFieldFace`'s signature is untouched. The accept set of the form widens only in what it recognises inside a served JSON Schema document (one vendor keyword the `JsonSchema` type already admitted as an arbitrary key); nothing objectui publishes moves.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/9830-erased-arm-mark.md`: `'@object-ui/app-shell': patch` — right. The diff is a behaviour fix inside one package with no exported symbol, prop, type or accepted input of objectui's own surface changing; Changeset Declaration, Bump Policy, Claim Re-read, Overwrite Report and Fixed Group Check all concluded success on the head. `Clause-②: no` — confirmed: the form reads a mark the served derivation already carries; no accept set that objectui publishes moves. The changeset prose matches the diff: it names the strict read (other type, other version, unmarked all keep the veto), the declaration tier winning both ways, no key-name rule, the four served rows that move faces and why, and that an older backend sees no change.

**The review face — the pending #9911 changeset.** `.changeset/9830-nested-anyof-predicate-string-arm.md` (unreleased) closes with "an empty schema (`{}`) is still not read as a string arm … the pin test asserts the husk still gets no builder". Judged acceptable to publish unedited, on four grounds: (a) both entries release in the same `@object-ui/app-shell` patch and are read together under one version heading; (b) this PR's entry names that entry and states the narrowing in its own words ("that entry's statement that the husk gets no condition builder now holds for an UNMARKED husk only"); (c) the older sentences stay literally true after this PR — a bare `{}` is still not a string arm (a marked arm is not an empty schema, it carries a keyword) and the pin still asserts the unmarked husk gets no builder; (d) that file is outside the claimed surface (`5904971362`: one changeset), and the dev handed the option to the seat rather than silently widening the diff. Not a FAIL finding. If the seat prefers the older body corrected in place, the one-sentence fix is: replace its last sentence's tail "and the pin test asserts the husk still gets no builder" with "and the pin test asserts an UNMARKED husk still gets no builder — a husk the served declaration marks as an erased string arm (metadata-protocol 17.5.0 on) is the follow-up entry for objectui#9830" — carried by the seat as a follow-up commit, not by this record.

The unlock (`5903942724`) asks the claim to "read one served `/meta/types`"; the projection is the body that route serves, the result was JSON round-tripped, the stub registry listed the 30 schema-bearing types by the two proper accessors, and the reading carries its own controls (the member itself and the envelope unmarked, the in-payload `ast` a bare `{}`, `field.defaultValue` unmarked, `action.visible` unmarked from the retry arm). 2. *Pending #9911 changeset narrower than it reads; carrier PM seat.* Answered in ② — acceptable as published; the fix sentence is named for the seat to carry if wanted.
